newsitem.title: USA: Calif. redevelopment agency are sound financially.
newsitem.headline: Calif. redevelopment agency are sound financially.

text.p: The vast majority of redevelopment agencies in California appear to be financially sound, but some may face fiscal challenges, according to a report by the California state Auditor.
The Bureau of State Audits said only one in 39 redevelopment agencies that it reviewed was experiencing significant financial difficulties as of June 30, 1995.
The audit concluded that most redevelopment agencies were sound financially and were in compliance with state legal requirements, but that "some may face fiscal challenges."
The audit found that property values in most redevelopment areas were growing at rates that were the same or faster than those for the cities where they are located.

State law does not require redevelopment agencies to report on the results of their efforts. As a result, the auditor's report said not enough information was available to evaluate the effectiveness of the redevelopment efforts.
The audit was prepared at the request of California's joint legislative audit committee.
Redevelopment agencies were designed to eliminate blight and revitalize communities.
